Definition: to draw together, i.e. close; by implication, to leap (by contracting the limbs); specifically, to die (from gathering up the feet)
BiblicalUsage: To shut or to leap is one word: do not harden your heart nor shut your hand from your poor brother, the psalmist asks whether God hath in anger shut up His tender mercies, and the beloved comes leaping upon the mountains, skipping upon the hills.
TheologicalSignificance: I take the shut hand and the leaping feet as the two directions of the heart, closed to a brother or open to the beloved.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
